newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPICS-CRIME HITS CAPE BID, ATHENS, ROME POSITIVE.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-CRIME HITS CAPE BID, ATHENS, ROME POSITIVE.

text.p: Cape Town, one of the early favourites to host the 2004 Olympics, has had its bid to stage Africa's first Summer Games hampered by a rampant crime problem according to the International Olympic Committee's evaluation report on Thursday.
Although there was no clear favourite in the IOC report, Athens and Rome received positive reviews comfirming them as front-runners.
The IOC said the five finalist cities from 11 candidates would be announced at a meeting on March 7 in Lausanne.
The winner will be named by the IOC on September 5, also in Lausanne.

The 11 candidate cities, all visited in recent mopnths by the evaluation commission, are Cape Town, Rome, Athens, Istanbul, Lille, St Petersburg, Stockholm, Seville, St Juan, Rio de Janeiro and Buenos Aires.
Athens, which felt it was snubbed by the IOC in its bid to host the 1996 Centennial Olympics, received a generally favourable report.
The IOC praised Athens's efforts to alleviate pollution but said the city had significant problems with airport access and transportation. However, extensive improvements were under way.
It made no specific mention of security problems and terrorism in Athens, major concerns in its earlier bid.
The Athens bid also enjoyed the strongest local support among its citizens with 96.4 per cent of the population in favour of staging the Games.

Stockholm, also once considered among the front-runners, had its bid damaged by a poll that said only 32 percent of the population were in support of staging the Olympics while 52 percent were against.

The report also noted that the people of Cape Town were not generally against hosting the Olympics but that many thought the city's candidature was permature, indicating that other priorities should prevail.
However, staging the Olympic Games in South Africa would create new jobs and help unify South Africans in its post-Apartheid period, the report added.
The evaluation commission said the biggest concern about the Cape Town bid was the city's serious crime problems.
It acknowledged that plans and a detailed strategy had been developed to improve security but added that their full implementation over the coming years would be a challenge.
Aside from concerns about traffic, the Rome bid had no glaring weaknesses.

The report noted that the location of the competition venues and other Olympic sites had been planned in such a way as not to add to the congestion and that everything was being done to meet the transportation challenge of the Olympic Games.
It was also noted that Rome already has many first class sporting facilities in place and excellent accommodation choices.
